items.stem: Given that √5 is irrational, prove that 7 + 6√5 is irrational.
items.markingKey: Suppose 7 + 6√5 = r, rational. Then √5 = (r − 7)/6, which is rational (closure of ℚ), contradicting that √5 is irrational. Hence 7 + 6√5 is irrational (3 marks: assumption 1, rearrangement 1, contradiction 1).

items.stem: Give examples to show that the product of two irrational numbers can be rational and can also be irrational. Use √5 in your examples.
items.markingKey: One rational example (1), one irrational example with reason (2).

items.stem: Aditi measures a circular plate: circumference ≈ 44 cm and diameter 14 cm, and says "π = C/d is a ratio, so π must be rational". (i) Find C/d to 3 decimal places. (ii) Explain the error in Aditi's reasoning. (iii) Why is 22/7 used in calculations? (iv) Is 22/7 more or less than π?
items.answer: (i) ≈ 3.142 (ii) C and d cannot both be integers; measured values are approximations, and π is irrational (iii) a convenient rational approximation (iv) more (22/7 = 3.1428… > 3.14159…)
